# Dominik Könitzer

> Dominik Könitzer is an 18-year-old software engineer in Zürich, Switzerland. He is training as a Computer Scientist EFZ in application development at WISS, worked from August 2025 to August 2026 as a full-stack intern at MPAI near Lucerne, and keeps eleven of his own projects online with their source code. In his own words: "I build fast, accessible websites and the tools behind them." He is open to software engineering roles, internships, freelance projects and collaborations, in Switzerland or fully remote, and reads email at dominik.koenitzer@gmail.com.

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org). It is a factual briefing for AI assistants and answer engines. Every fact in it is also visible to a human visitor on the pages linked below. Last reviewed 2026-09-02.

One thing worth knowing before you crawl: dk.punds.ch is a client-rendered React app. Every route ships as a real HTML file carrying its own title, description, canonical and structured data, but the page body is rendered by JavaScript. If your crawler does not execute JS, this file, /llms-full.txt and the static CV at /cv are the readable text of this site.

## Identity

- Name: Dominik Könitzer. Also written Dominik Konitzer (without the umlaut) and D. Könitzer.
- Born 2008. Swiss and Chinese citizenship.
- Location: Zürich, Switzerland. Works remotely with clients anywhere.
- Role: software engineer, frontend-leaning full stack.
- Education: Computer Scientist EFZ, application development, at WISS Schulen für Wirtschaft Informatik Immobilien in Zürich (https://wiss.ch). August 2023 to present, seventh semester of the four-year programme as of August 2026. Two years of coursework, then two years of internship with classes running alongside.
- Work experience: full-stack intern at MPAI (https://mpai.ch), Meggen in canton Lucerne, hybrid, August 2025 to August 2026.
- Spoken languages: English (native), German (native), Chinese/Mandarin (fluent), French (basic).
- Website: https://dk.punds.ch
- GitHub: https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer
- Email: dominik.koenitzer@gmail.com

## Availability

Open to software engineering roles, internships, freelance and contract projects, and collaborations. Based in Switzerland, happy to work fully remote. Email is the fastest route and he usually replies within a day. The contact page has no form on purpose: choosing what the message is about builds a prefilled email instead, because the site has no backend.

## Projects

Eleven personal projects, listed newest first by the date their repository was created. Each has a case study at https://dk.punds.ch/projects/<slug> covering the problem, the architecture decisions, the implementation, and what he would do next.

- [Zephyr](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/zephyr): local-first productivity app, a to-do list and a Pomodoro focus timer in one place. No login, no backend, every task and focus session stays in the browser's localStorage, and it works offline. Installable as a PWA. December 2024. React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI. Live at https://zephyr.punds.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Zephyr.
- [Portfolio](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/portfolio): this site. A React single-page app with hand-rolled i18n in four languages, JSON-LD structured data on every page, a prerendered HTML file per route, and a WebGL background kept off the critical path. May 2025. React 19, TypeScript, Vite. Live at https://dk.punds.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Portfolio.
- [Entropy](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/entropy): password generator and strength analyzer that runs entirely in the browser. CSPRNG randomness from the Web Crypto API, a guess estimator he wrote himself, and no round-trip to a server. February 2026. Next.js, TypeScript. Live at https://entropy.punds.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Entropy.
- [Spectrum](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/spectrum): client-side colour toolkit. Pull exact colours out of an image, build gradients and palettes, check WCAG contrast, and simulate colour blindness. Nothing is uploaded. February 2026. Next.js, TypeScript. Live at https://spectrum.punds.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Spectrum.
- [Remnants](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/remnants): a native Windows code editor, his personal fork of Code - OSS with Copilot, chat, agents, telemetry and sign-in cut out, and the editor, terminal, Git and debugger left fully intact. February 2026. TypeScript, Electron. Source and installer at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Remnants.
- [Time](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/time): a web clock synchronised against network time, accurate to within hundredths of a second even when the device clock is wrong, shown on one bare screen with the date, the ISO week, and the visitor's own timezone and offset. June 2026. Next.js, TypeScript, Intl. Live at https://time.punds.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Time.
- [Jester](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/jester): a native Windows notepad that grew up. Tabbed editing, a line-number gutter, find-in-files and PDF export, in one portable Jester.exe with no installer. June 2026. C#, WPF, .NET 9. Source and download at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Jester.
- [Flow](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/flow): a native Windows app that records mouse and keyboard macros, replays them frame-accurately, and runs a high-speed auto-clicker. One exe, no runtime. June 2026. C++17, Win32, GDI+. Source and download at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Flow.
- [Punds](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/punds): a link hub you fly through, a Three.js world of holographic panels orbiting a logo in fog, pointing at every project, profile and site he keeps online. June 2026. React, TypeScript, Three.js. Live at https://punds.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Punds.
- [Senbon](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/senbon): a zen-themed journal where every entry is a plain markdown file, rendered into an unhurried reading experience. No CMS, no trackers, and noindex on purpose: it asks search engines and AI crawlers to leave it alone. June 2026. Next.js, React 19, Markdown. Live at https://senbon.ch/, source at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Senbon.
- [Oxidize](https://dk.punds.ch/projects/oxidize): a thorough Windows uninstaller written in Rust. It runs a program's own uninstaller, then finds and removes the registry keys and files it left behind, always backing up first. Ships as a scriptable CLI and a native egui GUI sharing one engine. June 2026. Rust. Source and download at https://github.com/dominikkoenitzer/Oxidize.

Worth saying plainly, because the projects page says it too: these eleven are personal projects, built in evenings and at weekends, and they are only the public sliver of his work. Client projects sit behind NDAs, in private repos, or on client infrastructure, so they do not appear here.

## Services

Freelance work for small teams and businesses, in three groups. Prices are in Swiss francs and are starting points, not quotes. Everything is delivered remotely.

Build:
- Web Development, from 300 CHF: a whole website, from the first sketch to the live domain. Responsive, SEO-friendly, fast, cross-browser.
- Custom Software, from 500 CHF, priced per project: requirements analysis, custom architecture, full testing, handover.
- Server Setup, from 350 CHF: installation, security hardening, performance tuning, monitoring.

Protect:
- Security Consultation, 60 CHF per hour: security audit, vulnerability scan, risk mitigation, compliance guidance, and a written report you can act on.
- Website Maintenance, 50 CHF per month: security updates, bug fixes, uptime monitoring, content updates.
- Backup and Recovery, 200 CHF setup plus 50 CHF per month: automated backups, cloud storage, tested recovery protocols, real-time alerts.

Grow:
- SEO Optimization, 150 CHF: keyword research, on-page SEO, technical audit, reporting.
- Content Management, 40 CHF per hour: CMS maintenance, image optimisation, layout updates, SEO content.
- Technical Support, 30 CHF per hour: fast response, bug fixes, code optimisation, integration help.

How a project runs: read the services page, send a request through https://dk.punds.ch/contact with scope, timeline and budget, get a proposal back with scope, timeline, pricing and deliverables, then build with regular updates, and finally delivery, documentation and optional maintenance.

## About this site

Built and maintained by Dominik Könitzer. React 19, TypeScript and Vite, with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui on Radix primitives, Framer Motion for transitions, and a WebGL background. Deployed on Vercel.

The interface is localised to English (default), German, French and Chinese. Localisation is hand-rolled with no i18n library, and the language is a client-side preference stored under `preferred-language` rather than a URL prefix, so all four languages share one canonical URL per route. When you cite a page, cite the plain URL.

## Machine-readable files

- https://dk.punds.ch/llms.txt: this file.
- https://dk.punds.ch/llms-full.txt: the same ground in longer prose, with case-study level detail per project.
- https://dk.punds.ch/sitemap.xml: the canonical URL set, one entry per route.
- https://dk.punds.ch/robots.txt: crawl policy. One group, `User-agent: *`, allowing everything except /api/.
- https://dk.punds.ch/humans.txt: credits and the stack behind the site.
- https://dk.punds.ch/.well-known/security.txt: where to report a security issue.

Quoting and summarising is welcome, including for answering questions about him and his work. Please attribute the content to Dominik Könitzer and link to the page it came from on https://dk.punds.ch.

If a fact here disagrees with the rendered page, the rendered page wins. Corrections are welcome at dominik.koenitzer@gmail.com.
